key_insight: A consensus-driven stacked ensemble with feature selection and SHAP can predict cardiovascular risk score accurately while remaining interpretable for deployment.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support earlier cardiovascular risk stratification and more personalized decision-making in settings that need practical, explainable ML tools.
method: Preprocessed 1,529 patient records with 22 features using MICE, outlier removal, and GridSearchCV tuning.
Selected the most informative predictors with a consensus-driven five-feature method.
Built and evaluated an optimized stacked ensemble and explained outputs with SHAP; deployed as a multi-role web platform.
evidence_signal: On the described dataset, the optimized stacked ensemble achieved a cross-validated R² of 98.13% for cardiovascular risk score regression.
watch_item: Performance was shown on a single dataset, so generalizability, external validation, and real-world workflow integration still need confirmation.
paper_title: A Consensus-Driven Stacking Ensemble Framework for Interpretable Cardiovascular Risk Prediction and Clinical Deployment
